newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Crude - WTS up on knee-jerk reaction to Cano.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Crude - WTS up on knee-jerk reaction to Cano.

text.p: West Texas Sour/Midland (WTS) raced ahead early Tuesday on news of shipping disruptions to Colombian Cano Limon crude oil, even though traders said actual impact from delays should be minimal.
WTS traded initially at a $1.20 discount Tuesday then as low as $1.20 under benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, traders said.
"It's moved in on the Cano Limon story and it shouldn't have," said a trader for a major international oil company. "There was no news on it today and it shouldn't have an effect anyway," he added.

The Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline was bombed by rebels again on Tuesday, marking the 38th such attack this year. Force majeure on liftings of Cano Limon was declared on July 6 and state Ecopetrol declared force majeure on the field on Monday evening, a move which seems likely to affect project work there.

But traders have said that the temporary loss of the 180,000 barrels per day (bpd) production from the field, about 120,000 bpd of which was for export, should not have much affect in a Gulf of Mexico market awash with sour crude from such sources as Venezuela and Mexico.
"This is just knee-jerk stuff. It had started moving out last week and this probably is just some short-covering," said a Houston broker.

Meanwhile, WTI/Cushing was up about 20/25 cents mid-morning, following futures which traded higher on the back of firmer gasoline ahead of the weekly American Petroleum Institute report due out after markets close.
The report is expected to show a healthy draw in gasoline stocks last week.
Among other grades that traded Tuesday, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James changed hands at 20 cents over WTI.
"There are plenty of sellers above that. The North Sea programs (for August) were lower but not as low as people thought they would be," said an oil company trader.
LLS had been gaining over the last month, moving from a 25 cent discount to a 25 cent premium last week, in anticipation of lower North Sea imports to U.S.
Midland/WTI traded at a 25 cents discount, little changed.
Eugene Island, another sour crude, moved at a $1.35 discount Tuesday, also little changed.
